newsitem.title: GERMANY: Spinners seek old crop cotton in Bremen market.
newsitem.headline: Spinners seek old crop cotton in Bremen market.

text.p: European yarn spinners are looking for nearby cotton ahead of the new crop but transactions are limited by fading supply, a fortnightly report from the local Cotton Exchange said.
Buyers and sellers were unable to agree on new crop prices and this also slowed activity.
The firm dollar versus the mark added to sales quotes.
Spot sales were limited to Uzbek origins while nearby shipping dates were booked for Syrian, Indian and Paraguayan, West African and Central Asian supply.
Upland trades for fourth quarter 1997 through first half 1998 included the latter two origins, Sudan-Acala, Greek medium grades and Chadian cotton.
Cotton stocks as of August 1 totalled 58,792 bales compared with 49,061 bales a fortnight earlier and 84,901 bales a year earlier.
